p: Beyond the British Museum, Bloomsbury has some fascinating smaller museums that are perfect for an afternoon before your darts session. Sir John Soane's Museum on Lincoln's Inn Fields is the house of the architect who designed the Bank of England, packed floor to ceiling with art, antiquities and curiosities, and it's free to visit. The Foundling Museum tells the moving story of London's first home for abandoned children, and the Charles Dickens Museum on Doughty Street is where the great writer lived and worked.

For green space, Russell Square and Bedford Square are classic London squares, with trees and benches for a breather. Coram's Fields nearby is a lovely park specifically for children, where adults can only enter if accompanied by a child.

For your Flight Club session, a few tips. Book for the right number of players and arrive a few minutes early to settle in. If your group's big, split across two oches. Decide who's in charge of picking the games, and start with something simple before moving on to the more chaotic formats.

New to darts? Stand side-on with your front foot forward, keep your elbow steady and throw with your forearm. A smooth flick works better than a big throw. The scoring tech does all the maths, so you can concentrate on your aim and enjoying the banter with your group. Then it's back out into Bloomsbury for a late bite.
